text: The match between Kingsmoor FC and Westport Albion was super exciting with lots of goals! Viktor Quinlan scored two goals for Kingsmoor, one was a penalty and the other a clever shot after his team passed the ball many times nicely [#152] [#222]. Rafael Delacroix made two amazing goals for Westport with fast and smart plays [#401] [#553]. Both teams played hard; Kingsmoor liked to cross the ball from wide areas, while Westport used quick, straight passes [#222] [#553]. When Kingsmoor had one player less for a moment, they still scored a beautiful goal after a fast pass and cross by Mason Morales to Luca Iversen [#1495] [#1516]. The game finished with a 3-3 draw, making it one cool match to watch for fans! Imagine the ball flying like a rocket after a perfect cross into the box!

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for kid audience in en

- Viktor Quinlan scored 2 goals including a penalty with a combined xG of 0.957 [#152,#222].
- Rafael Delacroix scored 2 goals with a very high xG of 0.797 and 0.992, both from open play [#401,#553].
- Final score was a 3-3 draw between Kingsmoor FC and Westport Albion [final_score].
- Kingsmoor FC had 10 shots, 3 on target, with an xG of 3.3; Westport Albion had more shots (18) and shots on target (11) with xG of 3.41 [team_stats].
- Felix Barros received a second yellow card and was sent off at 81' when the score was 2-3 [#1495].

- Kingsmoor FC’s first goal came from a penalty, so it was a set piece situation rather than open-play tactical build-up [152].  
- The second Kingsmoor FC goal at 12’ arose after a ball regain and a sustained 8-pass sequence lasting 26.7 seconds, demonstrating patient build-up and exploiting their wide, crossing style aligned with the 4-4-2 formation emphasizing wide play and crossing options [222]. This suggests an overload pattern in possession phases.  
- Westport Albion’s two quick goals at 22’ and 30’ followed regains and involved vertical, direct passing typical of their 4-4-2 formation and style. The second goal included a cross from Dylan Rahman into a close-range finish by Rafael Delacroix, reflecting effective crossing within a direct attack [401,553].  
- The last Kingsmoor FC goal at 82’ was a quick attack starting from a regain, with just two passes and a cross assist by Mason Morales, catching Westport Albion in transition. This aligns with Kingsmoor’s wide, crossing attack style and suggests they exploited the man advantage after Westport’s red card at 81’ [1516,1495].  
- Tactical shifts show Kingsmoor pressed higher and played more direct from 65’, indicating attempts to increase pressing intensity and verticality to chase the game [1187]. Westport Albion, by contrast, dropped deeper and slowed the tempo from 79’, aiming to protect their lead by lowering pressing and defensive line height, consistent with a more cautious approach [1459].
